hints.title: Think in terms of a bottleneck
hints.body: For a fixed path, the time required is the maximum elevation on that path. You want the path whose maximum elevation is as small as possible.

hints.title: Test a water level
hints.body: For a candidate time `t`, cells with elevation at most `t` are passable. A breadth-first search tells you whether the destination is reachable at that level.

hints.title: Search the time
hints.body: Reachability only improves as `t` increases, so binary search the answer between the start elevation and the largest elevation. Alternatively, run a Dijkstra-style search that minimizes the maximum elevation seen so far.

hints.title: Pseudocode
hints.body:
```
low = grid[0][0], high = maximum elevation in grid
while low < high:
    mid = floor((low + high) / 2)
    if destination is reachable using cells <= mid:
        high = mid
    else:
        low = mid + 1
return low
```

The reachability check is a four-direction breadth-first search that refuses cells above the candidate level. This is pseudocode, not a complete implementation.
